newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska seeding progresses, needs rain and warmth.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska seeding progresses, needs rain and warmth.

text.p: Excellent weather aided Nebraska's planting progress in the week ended May 18 but dryness was a growing concern for the winter wheat crop, the state Agricultural Statistics Service said in a weekly update.
It said record low temperatures for this time of year were recorded in the state on Tuesday but most corn had not yet emerged and so the crop was not severely affected.

"Although dry weatherons were great for fieldwork, rain was needed to encourage crop emergence and grass growth. Southwestern wheat fields are in dire need of moisture," it said. "The effects of last week's freezing temperatures were still being evaluated. Much of the panhandle crop had not yet jointed at the time of the freeze," the agency added.

Winter wheat crop conditions fell sharply to 40 percent good to excellent, versus 56 percent at that level last week. The crop was rated 44 percent fair vs 38 pct last week abd 16 percent poor to very poor, versus 8 percent a week ago.
Wheat jointed 63 pct vs 44 week ago, 68 year ago, 84 on a 5-year average.
Wheat headed 1 pct vs nil w/a, 1 y/a, 10 avge.
Corn planted 94 pct vs 70 w/a, 82 y/a, 73 avge.
Corn emerged 40 pct vs 6 w/a, 38 y/a, 33 avge.
Soybeans planted 42 pct vs 5 w/a, 13 y/a, 23 avge.
Soybeans emerged 3 pct vs nil w/a, 1 y/a, 5 avge.
Sorghum planted 27 pct vs 5 w/a, 7 y/a, 16 avge.
Sorghum emerged 1 pct vs nil w/a, 0 y/a, 3 avge.
Pasture ratings fell in the week to 2 pct excellent, 48 pct good, 27 pct fair, 10 pct poor, and 3 pct very poor.
